clue.text: Master beginning break over the weekend?

indicators.note: The beginning of a word is the letter it starts with, so one opening letter is all that is taken from the word beside it.

parts.note: the opening letter of 'break'
o is the cricket scorer's short form for an over
Saturday and Sunday, each shortened to its own s

explanation.surface: Someone in charge taking a break for the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master beginning' reads as one phrase, a master making a start, when 'beginning' is an instruction belonging to the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is the person whose orders are followed at work, which is what 'master' means in the older employment sense.

clue.text: Single rebel royalist

indicators.note: A rebel refuses to keep to the order they are put in, and these letters refuse in exactly the same way.

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters, matching the enumeration

explanation.surface: A lone rebel who turns out to be on the crown's side after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Three words that read as one political portrait, so nothing looks like raw material until you count the letters of the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary means on its own with nothing beside it, so 'Single' is the lone-figure sense rather than the unmarried one.

clue.text: Club sacks woman with fringe

indicators.note: To sack somebody is to get rid of them, so the letter that stands for the word after it is dropped out.

parts.note: a wedge is the golf club you take to loft the ball
w is the standard short form of woman, as on a lavatory door, and it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A golf club dismissing a woman with a fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like the nightclub doing the sacking, and the word wanted is the one in a golf bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of a thing is its outer border, which is what a fringe is — the fringe of a wood is where it stops.

clue.text: Very angry man gets upset over independence

definitions.note: The answer looks like a verb's -ing form but is being used as a plain adjective here, the way British slang has it: he was steaming.

indicators.note: Somebody upset over a thing is thrown into a state about it, and letters in that state will not stay in the order given.

parts.note: seven letters of fodder, buried in a phrase that reads as plain narrative
i is the short form of independence, the tag an independent candidate carries

explanation.surface: A man losing his temper about a country going independent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very angry man' reads as one description, so 'man' looks like part of the definition rather than the first three letters of the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is British slang for furious, from the picture of somebody so hot with rage they give off steam.

clue.text: Doctor Who saves 50,500 in pit?

indicators.note: To doctor something is to tamper with it, so the word beside it comes out with its letters altered.
Saving a thing is keeping it safe inside you, so the letters named next are held within the tampered ones.

parts.note: three letters of fodder for the tampering the word in front asks for
read the digits in pairs: 50 is L in Roman numerals, then 50 again, then a nought written as o

explanation.surface: The Time Lord rescuing a large sum of money from down a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' looks like the Time Lord's name; the first word is an instruction and only the second is material. The comma in the number is the setter's, not arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a scooped-out dip in the ground, so 'pit' names it loosely: a pit is dug, a hollow simply sits there.

clue.text: Piece covering honour

parts.note: the chess piece that jumps in an L shape
a hood is the covering you pull up over your head

explanation.surface: A cloth laid over a medal so the award underneath cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece covering' reads as one thing draped over another, and the middle word is not an instruction: nothing goes inside anything here.
explanation.definitionFit: A knighthood is the rank the monarch confers with a sword, so 'honour' names it as one of the entries on the honours list.

clue.text: Against German city scrapping new large ship

indicators.note: Scrapping something is throwing it out, so the letter standing for the word after it is thrown out of the name before.

parts.note: v is versus in a fixture list, the two sides set against each other
Essen is the industrial city in the Ruhr
n is the standard short form of new, and it is the letter thrown out
l is the size on a clothing label

explanation.surface: Objecting to a German city that is breaking up a big new ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapping new large ship' reads as a breaker's yard at work, which is where the setter wants your eye while those words do three separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any craft that goes on water, so a 'ship' is one of them — the word covers everything from a dinghy upwards.

clue.text: Remain close to boats on river

indicators.note: The close of a word is where it finishes, so only the final letter of the word beside it is used.

parts.note: the final letter of 'boats'
the Tay is the long Scottish river that runs out past Dundee

explanation.surface: Mooring right up against the boats on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to boats' reads as a position on the water, and 'close' is wanted in its other sense, the end of a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain where you are: 'remain seated' and 'stay seated' ask for the same thing.

clue.text: Like 0, nothing (0) divides 51500

parts.note: nothing is written as a nought, and a nought on the page is the letter o

indicators.note: To divide a thing is to come between its parts, so the letter named goes into the middle of what follows and splits it.

parts.note: the digits break into Roman numerals: 5 is V, 1 is I, 500 is D
the bracketed nought is a second o, and it is the one that goes in

explanation.surface: A note about zero going into a five-figure number.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(0)' looks like a helpful gloss on the word in front of it and is a second nought in its own right, while the definition is the shape of the numeral itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, and a written 0 is drawn as that same closed oval, so 'Like 0' points at the shape.

clue.text: It's not her fault being most difficult

indicators.note: A fault is a break, the crack that runs through rock, and letters broken like that come out in a new order.

parts.note: nine letters of fodder, and the apostrophe is not one of them

explanation.surface: Somebody insisting a woman is not the one to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's not her fault' is a complete sentence of excuse, which is exactly why none of it looks like material waiting to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is a prickly, awkward one, so the superlative is the hardest of them all — superlative for superlative.

clue.text: One secures Milligan no trouble

parts.note: Spike Milligan, the Goon Show comedian, went by that first name
n is the short form of 'no.', the number sign
what ails you is what troubles you

explanation.surface: Somebody landing the comedian with no bother at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no trouble' reads as how easily the job went, and each of its two words is a separate piece of the build.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike-nail is the long heavy nail driven through timbers to fasten them, so 'One secures' names it by the job it does.

clue.text: Bubbly girl in Germany on vacation, not Luxembourg

indicators.note: 'In' puts one thing inside another, so the letters named before it sit within the word that follows.
A house on vacation stands empty, so the word keeps only the letters at its two ends and loses everything between.

parts.note: emptied out, the country's name keeps only its first and last letters

indicators.note: 'Not' cancels what comes after it, so the letter standing for the country named there is taken away.

parts.note: a lass is a girl, in the northern English word
l is Luxembourg's international plate letter, and it is the letter taken away

explanation.surface: A cheerful girl holidaying in Germany, though not going on to Luxembourg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly girl' reads as one description of a lively person, and those two words end up on opposite sides of the clue's join.
explanation.definitionFit: A gassy drink is full of bubbles, so 'Bubbly' is the fizz sense of the word and not the personality one.

clue.text: Tea includes some butter and bread

indicators.note: To include a thing is to have it inside you, so the letters named next sit within the word before.

parts.note: chai is tea, the spiced Indian kind
a pat is the small square of butter that comes with a roll

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea with butter and bread laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea' wants to be the drink on the tray, and the word needed is the Indian one — which is also where the bread on the plate comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is the flat unleavened bread cooked on a griddle in Indian kitchens, so 'bread' is the plain category word for it.

clue.text: Church wing's appeal

parts.note: ch is the standard short form of church, as printed on an old map
an arm of an organisation is a wing of it — the political arm, the political wing

explanation.surface: The pull that one wing of a church has for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church wing' reads as a part of a building, and the second word wants the sense used of a party's wing rather than any architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is the appeal a person or place exerts: 'the charm of the village' and 'the appeal of the village' say one thing.

clue.text: Perhaps Dame Edna is a natural disaster

indicators.note: A disaster leaves everything strewn about, and the letters beside it land in a heap in some order of their own.

parts.note: ten letters of fodder, sitting where the sentence sounds like praise

explanation.surface: Somebody remarking that Dame Edna is a born catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natural disaster' is a set phrase — earthquake, flood — and the setter splits it in two, so the second word becomes an instruction about the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edna Everage, Barry Humphries's gladioli-waving housewife, is from Melbourne, and 'Perhaps' flags her as one example of the nationality.

clue.text: Country imports dry fencing material

definitions.note: The answer is plural and 'fencing material' is a mass noun: a fence's worth of them is spoken of as material rather than counted one by one.

indicators.note: A country that imports something brings it in over its border, so the letters named next go inside the country's name.

parts.note: the country on England's western side
tt is teetotal, the mark of somebody who takes no drink

explanation.surface: A nation bringing in dry goods to build fences with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry fencing material' reads as one order from a builders' merchant, and 'dry' is the abstinence sense rather than anything about the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattles are the woven rods that make hurdle fencing, so 'fencing material' names them by what they are for.

clue.text: Floor to ceiling, hell's in gloom

indicators.note: in a down answer the floor is the bottom letter, and moving it to the ceiling puts it at the top

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth, a name for hell

explanation.surface: A building's gloomy interior, floor to ceiling, feels like hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor to ceiling' takes the last S of HADES, the bottom of the down light, and lifts it to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Shade is partial darkness out of the light, so gloom is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Sailor's ship crossing unknown gulf

indicators.note: To cross into a place is to go inside it, so the letter named next is set among the pieces around it.

parts.note: ab is able seaman, the rating a sailor holds
ss is the prefix on a steamship's name
y is the algebra teacher's unknown, standing alongside x

explanation.surface: A sailor's ship crossing a gulf nobody has charted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor's ship' reads as one possession, the vessel he serves in, and the two words are separate pieces of the build.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulf is the unbridgeable gap in 'a gulf between them', which is the bottomless sense the answer carries.

clue.text: On retreat, say love of the earth

indicators.note: An army in retreat turns and goes back the way it came, so the letters beside it are written in the opposite order.

parts.note: love is a score of nothing at tennis, written as a nought
'say' is eg, for example, and here it is turned round

explanation.surface: Somebody away on a retreat, professing love of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On retreat, say' reads as a hedge, the way people say 'so to speak', and 'say' is the piece being turned rather than a softener.
explanation.definitionFit: Geo- is the combining form meaning earth, from the Greek ge: geology and geography are both studies of it.

clue.text: Where to find fruit tea lined by gold roads

indicators.note: A thing lined by something has that something running along it on either side, so the word before sits between the two pieces named next.

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry, the tincture on a shield
the plural of the rd on a street sign
cha is tea in the old British slang, borrowed from the Chinese word

explanation.surface: A place selling fruit tea, reached along roads lined with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit tea' is the trap: the definition stops at 'fruit' and the next word belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchards are the plantations where fruit trees are grown, so the definition points at them as the place fruit comes from.

clue.text: The final of some game shown

indicators.note: What is shown is already on display, so these letters need no changing: they are sitting in view in the words beside it.

parts.note: five letters in a row, starting partway through the first word and running over the gap

explanation.surface: The last of some game being televised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The final of some game' reads as a cup tie, and the answer is a Greek letter rather than a match: the last one in that alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega ends the Greek alphabet, so 'The final' names it by position — the phrase 'the alpha and the omega' turns on that.

clue.text: Corrupt police wanting Conservative government to reverse EU's conclusion

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the remaining letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so the letter is taken out of the word police
to reverse means the two letters of the European Union abbreviation are turned round

parts.note: EU is the European Union; the 's joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: Bent police with no Tory government in charge make Brussels turn tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting Conservative' leaves POLIE, which 'Corrupt' reshuffles to EPILO; G follows, then EU 'to reverse' gives UE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing section of a book or play, the part that forms its conclusion.

clue.text: In Ireland, my dear, telecom company completes high speed runs

indicators.note: To complete a thing is to supply its last part, so the letters named beside it go on the end rather than the front.

parts.note: mach numbers measure speed at and beyond the speed of sound
r is runs on a cricket scorecard
EE is the British mobile network, once Everything Everywhere

explanation.surface: A phone company finishing its high-speed rollout across Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase, an Irish endearment, and 'completes' is quietly an instruction rather than a word about the rollout.
explanation.definitionFit: Machree is the Irish-English endearment from mo chroi, 'my heart', used exactly where an English speaker says 'my dear'.

clue.text: The King asks 'Why guard that woman's virginity?'

parts.note: cr is Carolus Rex, the cypher the present king signs with

indicators.note: A guard stands round whatever it protects, so the letters named after it go inside the pieces before.

parts.note: the letter is named aloud in the king's question: say it and you have said the whole of it
'her' is the possessive that belongs to a woman being pointed at

explanation.surface: A king demanding to know why one woman's virginity needs guarding.
explanation.walkthrough: Quotation marks and a question mark paint a whole scene at court, and the quoted word is one letter said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is the slang term for virginity, as in losing your cherry, so the definition is that colloquial sense rather than the fruit.

clue.text: Curried lamb follows starter of egg and finally plum preserve

indicators.note: follows means the curried lamb comes after the two single letters
the starter of a word is its opening letter, here the first of egg

parts.note: E is the first letter of egg

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word plum

parts.note: M is the last letter of plum

indicators.note: curried, like a cooked dish whose ingredients are mixed together, means the letters of lamb are rearranged

explanation.surface: A menu: curried lamb after an egg starter, then a plum preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter of' egg gives E and 'finally' plum gives M; the lamb is 'Curried' into BALM, which 'follows' them.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to treat it so it is preserved from decay.

clue.text: Drug lines captured by film

indicators.note: Something captured is held fast inside its captor, so the letters named first go within the word named after.

parts.note: cine is the film word — a cine camera shoots moving pictures
an ode is a set of lines, a poem written in praise of something

explanation.surface: A dealing line caught on a surveillance camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug lines' reads as one thing, the dealing network the camera catches, and the split falls after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is the opiate painkiller in cough medicine, so 'Drug' names it by its class.

clue.text: Magic time

definitions.meaning: the words a witch says over a cauldron to make something happen
a stretch of it — a cold one, or one served at His Majesty's pleasure

explanation.surface: A time that was pure magic.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words that read as one phrase, a magical stretch of time, are two definitions standing side by side with nothing joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a form of words that works magic, and also a period of time — a cold spell, a spell in prison.

clue.text: Male to talk about employing technical leader

indicators.note: employing means the reversed word takes on, and so holds, the extra letter
about means turned round, so the word for talk is read backwards

parts.note: to gas is to talk at length

indicators.note: the leader of technical is its first letter

parts.note: T is the first letter of technical

explanation.surface: A man is asked to talk about hiring someone to head the technical side.
explanation.walkthrough: GAS read 'about' is SAG, which goes 'employing' T, the 'leader' of technical, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and the word is also used for a man on his own, as in a stag party.

clue.text: Where executives are allegedly uninterested by discharge

indicators.note: 'Allegedly' says the words are only being reported, and a reported word is one you hear rather than see spelled.

parts.note: uninterested is bored, and said aloud that is also the company's body of directors
rheum is the watery discharge from the eyes and nose, and it sounds exactly like the word for a space

explanation.surface: Directors said to be unmoved by some medical discharge.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are heard rather than spelled, and the second turns on rheum, a word few people meet outside a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The boardroom is where a company's directors sit, so 'Where executives are' names it by its occupants.

clue.text: Drop down tree

parts.note: d is the short form of down, as on this puzzle's own clue list
the ash is the tall tree with the black buds

explanation.surface: A tree coming down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop down' reads as one movement, the way a branch falls, and those two words sit on opposite sides of the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash of milk is a drop of it, the small splash you put in tea, so both words are that same noun.

clue.text: To hide tiara from bank robbers ends in calamity

indicators.note: The end of a word is its final letter, and one is taken from each of the words listed before.
A calamity leaves everything in a heap, so those four letters come out in an order of their own.

parts.note: the last letter of each of the four words, taken in the order they come

explanation.surface: Keeping a tiara out of the hands of bank robbers, and it all going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends in calamity' reads as how the story finished, and those three words carry both the letter-picking and the shuffle that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to hide it behind a covering, so 'To hide' matches it verb for verb, infinitive for infinitive.

clue.text: Sent flying, high admiral tours Italy and Spain

indicators.note: Somebody high is not in charge of themselves, and letters in that condition come out in any order but their own.
A tour goes round from country to country, so the two letters named after it are picked up and carried into the shuffle.

parts.note: seven letters of fodder, more than two thirds of the enumeration
i is Italy's international plate letter
e is Spain's international plate letter, for Espana

explanation.surface: A tipsy admiral on a tour of Italy and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent flying' reads as a punch landing, and it is the postal sense instead: carried by plane rather than knocked across a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airmailed has been sent by air, so 'Sent flying' is the postman's flying rather than the boxer's.

clue.text: Call for help preserves university lecturer's spirits

indicators.note: To preserve a thing is to keep it, and what is kept is kept inside, so the letters named next go within the piece before.

parts.note: sos is the distress signal, three letters tapped out in Morse
u is the standard short form of university, as in a degree title
l is the standard short form of lecturer on a staff list

explanation.surface: A distress call saving the spirits of a university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'university lecturer' reads as one job title and is two separate letters, one taken from each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Souls are people's spirits, the immortal part of them: 'not a soul there' counts people by it, plural for plural.
